commands.review_summary:
The PR changes Comfy network policy generation to use shared exact-origin SSRF policy for local service hostnames and explicit private-DNS origins, removes manual cloud redirect handling, and adds docs plus regression tests.

PR surface: Source -16, Tests +523, Docs +4. Total +511 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level: current main sets local-mode private-network intent, but the Comfy policy gate rejects DNS hostnames before creating a policy, so the shared guard blocks private DNS answers.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] There is a narrow mechanical repair for the current-head type failure, while maintainer/security acceptance remains a separate merge gate.

target.title: fix(comfy): allow private service hostnames
target.body:
## Summary

- What problem this solves: Comfy local workflows could not use Docker/Compose service hostnames such as `http://comfyui:8188`, and private-DNS FQDNs needed explicit operator trust without broad SSRF authority.
- Why this change was made: the shared SSRF guard resolves DNS and owns redirect handling, so the Comfy plugin should grant private-origin trust only to the configured origin and let redirected destinations be re-evaluated by the guard.
- User impact: users can configure stable local service names and explicitly trusted private-DNS Comfy endpoints without allowing metadata/link-local destinations or private redirects outside the configured origin.
- Intended outcome: local loopback/private literals and single-label service names work implicitly; public-looking local private-DNS FQDNs and cloud private endpoints require `allowPrivateNetwork: true`; trust remains scoped to the configured scheme, hostname, and port.
- Out of scope: no config migration, no broader SSRF policy changes, and no live ComfyUI workflow changes.
- Reviewer focus: exact-origin SSRF policy construction in `resolveComfyNetworkPolicy()` and shared-guard redirect behavior for Comfy output downloads.

## Linked context

Closes #77922.

Requested by a maintainer/user through the handoff for the myagents Comfy provider setup.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Comfy provider SSRF policy construction and output redirect handling for service-discovery/private-DNS hostnames.
- Real environment tested: local source checkout on Node 24. The Comfy HTTP responses, DNS answers, and redirects are test-controlled; no secrets or live ComfyUI instance were used.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/comfy`
  - `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/comfy/test-helpers.ts`
  - `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check docs/providers/comfy.md`
  - `git diff --check`
  - `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --base upstream/main`
- Evidence after fix: targeted image-provider tests passed with 28 tests; full Comfy extension tests passed with 5 files and 42 tests; oxlint, docs format check, and whitespace check passed; final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Observed result after fix: local single-label hostnames resolving to RFC1918 are allowed; local public-looking FQDNs resolving private are blocked unless explicitly opted in; explicit private-DNS origins are allowed but metadata/link-local answers remain blocked; local redirects cannot leave the configured hostname; cloud redirects to public CDNs are allowed under strict redirect policy; cloud redirects to private or metadata destinations are blocked.
- Before evidence: the added regression tests failed against the previous PR state for broad policy shape, metadata/link-local resolution, same-host alternate private ports, public-CDN redirect handling, and local public-FQDN redirect boundaries.
- What was not tested: the original Docker Compose/myagents stack and a live ComfyUI service were not run from this checkout.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: Blacksmith Testbox could not run because the `blacksmith` CLI is unavailable; AWS Crabbox fallback could not run because the broker login is not configured. Focused local fallback proof was used instead.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/comfy`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/comfy/workflow-runtime.ts extensions/comfy/image-generation-provider.test.ts extensions/comfy/test-helpers.ts`
- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check docs/providers/comfy.md`
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --base upstream/main`

Regression coverage added:

- Local single-label hostname resolving to RFC1918 is allowed.
- Local public-looking FQDN resolving private is blocked without explicit opt-in.
- Local private-DNS FQDN with explicit `allowPrivateNetwork: true` is allowed.
- Trusted private-DNS hostname resolving to metadata/link-local is blocked.
- Local redirects to a subdomain, different hostname, same-host private alternate port, or public CDN hostname are blocked.
- Explicit private cloud origin redirecting to a public CDN is allowed under strict redirect policy.
- Cloud redirect to another private or metadata destination is blocked.

Known failure before this fix:

- `http://comfyui:8188` did not get a usable SSRF policy because `comfyui` is not an IP literal or `localhost`, so the shared fetch guard blocked it after DNS resolved it to the Compose private network.

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? `Yes`

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? `Yes`

Highest-risk area: SSRF policy construction and redirect handling for Comfy provider network calls.

Risk mitigation: private-network trust uses the shared exact-origin policy instead of suffix allowlisting or broad private-network allow; local mode also keeps a hostname allowlist so redirects cannot leave the configured hostname; cloud redirects are consumed by `fetchWithSsrFGuard` and rechecked at each destination.

## Current review state

Next action: maintainer review and CI.

Still waiting on: PR CI and optional live Docker Compose/ComfyUI proof if reviewers want product-level confirmation.

Bot/reviewer comments addressed: maintainer report feedback on exact-origin trust, manual cloud redirect handling, required regressions, docs, and #77922 link.
